topics.label: Welcome and Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning objectives and frames cancer as an evolutionary process shaped by mutations and the microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic Selection and Epigenetic Reprogramming in Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how clonal fitness and progression are driven by Darwinian selection of driver mutations as well as non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how hierarchical tissue organization, stemness properties, and specific cells of origin govern tumor initiation in leukemia and colorectal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Promotion of Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental exposures and chronic inflammation act as promotional signals to enable malignant transformation in mutated tissues.

topics.label: Established Microenvironments, Spatial Profiling, and Coevolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the stromal dependencies of established tumors, the spatial profiling tools used to analyze them, and an overarching synthesis of cancer coevolution.

topics.label: Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
